questions.reason: The only evidence is "When you sign up for Nebius Token Factory, a personal organization is created automatically.", which says nothing about spending budget alerts or hard credit caps; the captured page contains no mention of budgets, caps or billing at all, so the correct option is unsupported.

"Resources—such as models, endpoints, files, and datasets—exist inside a project and inherit its access settings.", together with "Each Project ... acts as an isolated environment", makes the project the isolating level.

"When you sign up for Nebius Token Factory, a personal organization is created automatically." supports option d; option c is excluded because the page puts the organization above projects rather than creating it on invitation.

"Within a project, you can create and manage: API keys, Fine-tuning jobs, Dedicated endpoints, Files and datasets" names projects as the containing level, and the organization is documented as containing projects, groups and user accounts.
"When you sign up for Nebius Token Factory, a personal organization is created automatically." states the automatic personal organization; no ticket, sandbox or agreement appears on the page.

The sole excerpt, "exist inside a project and inherit its access settings.", says nothing about the permissions needed to create dedicated endpoints; the correct option's claim of "project administrator or endpoint management write permissions" is invented beyond the captured page.

The page states the automatic personal organization and then "You can also be invited to other organizations and collaborate on their projects.", which supports option a and refutes the permanent-lock distractor.

"Each Project within an organization acts as an isolated environment for related resources and teams." plus resources that "exist inside a project and inherit its access settings" match option d and contradict the other three.
"When you sign up for Nebius Token Factory, a personal organization is created automatically." supports option a; the enterprise, sandbox and 24-hour-trial options have no basis on the page.

"Each project includes Project Groups that control access to project resources." supports option b, and "To grant a user access to organizational resources, add them to the relevant Organization Group." keeps Organization Groups at the wrong scope for the stem.

superseded.reason: The captured `GET /v1/models` parameter schema reads "name: verbose ... type: boolean / default: false / title: Verbose", which establishes `false` as the default and rules out the other three literals.

RerankResult documents `relevance_score` with "Relevance score of the document"; `total_tokens` (RerankUsage), `embedding` and `owned_by` belong to other schemas on other pages, so only one option fits.

"Reranks documents based on their relevance to a query." names the ranking operation, and the three distractors are each excluded by their own captured summaries (embed input text, create a model response for a chat conversation, list available models).
EmbeddingRequest ends with "required: - model - input"; encoding_format (default float), dimensions and user are all documented as optional on the same page.

`dimensions` is documented as "The dimensions to use for the request." with integer examples 4096 and 8192, while encoding_format is explicitly "The format to return the embeddings in. Can be either float or base64" and service_tier is a priority setting, so only `dimensions` sets vector size.

system_fingerprint is described as "This fingerprint represents the backend configuration that the model runs with.; Can be used in conjunction with the `seed` request parameter to understand when backend changes have been made that might impact determinism.", matching option a exactly.
RerankRequest lists "required: - model - query - documents"; user is "A unique identifier representing your end-user" and service_tier defaults to auto, both optional.

The `stream` description reads "Tokens will be sent as data-only [server-sent events](...) as they become available, with the stream terminated by a `data: [DONE]` message.", which only option a states.

The temperature description states "Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic."; the page promises no byte-identical output and does not say top_p is disabled.
"Local SSD disks are ephemeral, meaning temporary: their data is erased when the VM is stopped or deleted." directly settles the stopped-overnight case against every other option.

"One shared filesystem can be attached to multiple VMs at once." supports option d, and the same page rules out option a with "One Compute network SSD disk can only be added to one running VM at a time."
"The size of each namespace is 93 GiB, so the disk size must be a multiple of 93 GiB." explains the rejection of 100 GiB; no other option is grounded in the page.

"All VMs that the filesystem is attached to must belong to the same project. Sharing a filesystem across projects is not supported, even if the projects are in the same region." makes option c the only defensible answer and kills the same-tenant distractor.

"When you or the autoscaler scales a node group up or down, Managed Kubernetes does not recreate any nodes." supports option a verbatim and contradicts the replacement and drain-and-recreate distractors.
The max_tokens description ends "If omitted or set to null, defaults to 8192 tokens."; 100 appears only under `examples` and 1 is the default for `n`.
RerankResult requires index, document and relevance_score, with "Relevance score of the document", matching option c; no vector, rewrite or completion is returned.
The chat page's Usage schema defines completion_tokens, prompt_tokens and "Total number of tokens used in the request (prompt + completion).", exactly option a.

"To view an extended list of model parameters via the API, send a request to the List models endpoint with the query parameter `verbose=true`.", and the models schema does carry "context_length: type: integer".
"Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic." identifies temperature; the distractors are not model parameters.
